mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks (-18.0 to -10.9), exhibiting positive momentum consistent with an ongoing reopening-driven retail recovery that should continue over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean is lower than its trailing 28-day mean despite three consecutive weeks of prior increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility (70.1 to 58.4, -11.7 points) signals saturation of outdoor leisure activity, causing displaced consumer demand to shift toward retail and shopping venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to decline by more than 10 points but RETAIL_REC's next 2-week mean does not rise relative to the prior 2-week mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Lombardy's reopening regime (yellow-zone easing as of June 2021) combined with a partial WORKPLACES recovery signals ongoing policy loosening that will progressively raise retail footfall over the next four weeks as commercial restrictions continue to ease.
evidence_refs: fact:Lombardy in reopening phase as of 2021-06-15
failure_condition: If the reopening regime persists and WORKPLACES stays flat or declines further, yet RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery of TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility (commuting-linked activity) interacts to reinforce lunchtime and after-work retail visits, producing a larger RETAIL_REC increase over two weeks than either series would predict individually.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise in the same week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise concurrently but RETAIL_REC's growth over the following two weeks is no greater than during periods without joint rises, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Declining RESIDENTIAL mobility below 3 percent signals reduced home-bound behavior, indicating increased out-of-home activity including shopping trips, which should boost RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 3 percent in a given week
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls below 3 percent but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the subsequent week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Early-summer seasonal surge in outdoor recreation (PARKS sustained above 58 percent) persists and diverts consumer time and spending away from indoor retail venues, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks despite broader mobility normalization.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS exceeded 58-70 percent above baseline over the last three weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS remains elevated above 50 percent yet RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean rises above its trailing 28-day mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent deep suppression of TRANSIT mobility (around -25 to -28 percent) despite broader reopening signals continued public caution around enclosed shared transport, which limits cross-town retail trips and caps RETAIL_REC recovery over the next two weeks.
regime_hint: partial reopening with lingering transit caution
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains below -25 percent yet RETAIL_REC's 2-week forward mean rises materially above the trailing mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC indicate broad-based normalization of in-person consumer mobility beyond essential trips, a combined signal that reinforces further RETAIL_REC growth over the following week more strongly than either series alone.
candidate_trigger: both GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC rise in the same week
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC rise together in a given week but RETAIL_REC declines in the following week, the hypothesis fails.
